tidylandmark

Provides a tidy framework for landmark survival analysis, facilitating the construction of landmark-specific risk sets, incorporation of longitudinal covariates, and estimation of associations with time-to-event outcomes. Supports covariate estimation using last observation carried forward (LOCF) or linear mixed-effects models (LME), alongside Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Offers a consistent and reproducible workflow for conducting analyses across multiple landmark times.

Development

You can install the development version of tidylandmark from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("thatoneguy006/tidylandmark")

Use

We illustrate the package’s functionality with a basic example using data from the Mayo Clinic primary biliary cirrhosis trial. This data was originally bundled with the survival package as survival::pbcseq. We have included a copy of this data split across two datasets, pbcseq_baseline and pbcseq_visits for baseline/status and follow-up visits, respectively.

The data files include information on 312 randomized patients. Patients are followed after enrollment and have statuses of 0 = Censored, 1 = Received Transplant, or2 = Died. A sample of baseline patient characteristics and final status is shown below:

library(tidylandmark)
head(pbcseq_baseline)
#>   id trt      age sex futime status
#> 1  1   1 58.76523   f    400      2
#> 2  2   1 56.44627   f   5169      0
#> 3  3   1 70.07255   m   1012      2
#> 4  4   1 54.74059   f   1925      2
#> 5  5   0 38.10541   f   1505      1
#> 6  6   0 66.25873   f   2503      2

Construct Landmark Risk Sets

Data preparation for landmarking is first performed with the landmark_data function, which constructs the various landmark risk sets and included baseline covariates.

Here, we specify a landmark analysis setup where we aim to estimate from landmarks at approximately one through five years post-enrollment. In this example, we are interested in the six-month period after each landmark time and thus specify horizon = 180.

A summary of the landmark analysis set-up is printed along with the output, indicating the landmark times, number at risk at the landmark time, and the number censored or having events before the horizon, if specified.


# Construct landmark risk sets
lm_dat <- pbcseq_baseline |>
  landmark_data(
    id = id,
    time = futime,
    status = status,
    landmarks = 365 * 1:5,
    horizon = 180
  )

# Print summary of risk set specifications
lm_dat
#> <landmark_tbl> 5 landmark(s): 365, 730, 1095, 1460, 1825
#> Horizon: 180 (relative to each landmark)
#> Subjects: 290 at risk in current rows (312 in source data)
#> Source columns: id = id, time = futime, status = status

#>       730       278        260         4        14
#>      1095       245        237         0         8
#>      1460       225        218         2         5
#>      1825       202        194         3         5

A tidy method is also available yielding a tibble containing landmark risk set summaries.


# Pull risk set summaries as a tibble
lm_dat |>
  tidy(show_proportion = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   landmark prop_at_risk n_at_risk n_censored n_event_1 n_event_2
#>      <dbl>        <dbl>     <int>      <int>     <int>     <int>
#> 1      365        0.929       290        285         1         4
#> 2      730        0.891       278        260         4        14
#> 3     1095        0.785       245        237         0         8
#> 4     1460        0.721       225        218         2         5
#> 5     1825        0.647       202        194         3         5
